ai.description: This small shrub frog reaches 22–25 mm. It is brownish-grey with a distinct dark interorbital bar, white-spotted flanks, and granular skin. It lacks vomerine teeth and has a rounded snout.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Raorchestes kakkayamensis* is best distinguished by the prominent, distinct white spots on its dark-colored flanks and groin, which contrast sharply with its body pattern.
ai.habitat: The Kakkayam Shrub Frog inhabits the evergreen forests of the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations between 700 and 900 meters.
ai.behavior: The Kakkayam Shrub Frog is strictly nocturnal, spending its nights foraging for small insects among the foliage of the Western Ghats' evergreen forests.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Raorchestes kakkayamensis* exhibits direct development, bypassing the tadpole stage. They lay small clutches of eggs in leaf axils during the monsoon (June–August).
ai.distributionRemarks: The Kakkayam Shrub Frog is endemic to the Kakkayam region of the Western Ghats in Kerala, India, typically found at elevations around 750 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Kakkayam Shrub Frog produces a series of high-pitched, metallic "tink-tink" notes, typically heard emanating from dense vegetation within its humid forest habitat.
